content.text:
I have the brief. Let me analyze the prior constellation before deciding.

**Key findings from the prior data (all PE+lead slab designs):**
- Neutron dose (R2) is driven almost entirely by polyethylene thickness; photon dose (R3) is driven almost entirely by lead thickness (removing all lead causes R3 to fail by 3-4x even at max PE thickness).
- The lightest **fully verified pass** in the prior sweep is **105 cm polyethylene + 5 cm lead**: mass 1554 kg, thickness 110 cm, R2 CI [2.97, 6.63] (vs 7 limit — tight, ~5% margin), R3 CI [1.17, 1.28] (vs 3 limit — comfortable, ~57% margin), all PASS.
- 100 cm PE + 5 cm lead is one step lighter but R2 goes "inconclusive" ([6.57, 10] straddles the 7 limit) — too risky to rely on.
- Removal cross-sections in the material table (PE 0.110/cm, Pb 0.118/cm) let me back out an approximate exponential model consistent with the prior trend, which I use to reason about small, physically-justified trims beyond the tested points.

Given this is a single-shot submission with no feedback, I'm building a small portfolio: one candidate identical to the best proven prior design (highest confidence), one modest physically-reasoned trim that should still hold comfortable margins, and one already-verified higher-margin fallback.

# No-iterative-feedback designer arm (arm C)

3 candidate(s) submitted in one call; none evaluated in this session.

| candidate | design | rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| c-0000 | 105 cm polyethylene + 5 cm lead | This design is identical to the lightest fully-passing configuration in the prior Core-scored constellation: mass 1554 kg/m^2, thickness 110 cm. Prior data show R1-screen=1 (pass), R2-neutron CI [2.97,6.63] (fully below the 7 uSv/h allocation), R3-photon CI [1.17,1.28] (fully below the 3 uSv/h allocation), R4-mass 1554 kg (below 2000 kg cap), R5-thickness 110 cm (below 120 cm cap), and R6-activation ~5.8e-5 Bq/g (far below 1 Bq/g). The next lighter tested point (100 cm PE + 5 cm Pb) went inconclusive on R2 (CI [6.57,10] straddling the limit), so 105+5 is the lightest point in the prior sweep with a confirmed clean pass on every requirement. This is my highest-confidence candidate and matches the prior record on mass (no regression, verified reliability). |
| c-0001 | 106 cm polyethylene + 4 cm lead | An attempt to trim below the prior record (1554 kg) to ~1450 kg (~6.7% lighter) by trading 1 cm of lead for 1 cm of polyethylene. Using the removal cross sections in the material table (PE 0.110/cm, Pb 0.118/cm), the total neutron removal exponent for 106 PE + 4 Pb (0.110*106+0.118*4=12.13) is essentially unchanged from the proven-pass 105 PE + 5 Pb baseline (exponent 12.14), so R2-neutron should remain comfortably passing near its prior CI of roughly [2.9,6.6]. For photon shielding, isolating the lead contribution from the 115-cm-PE prior rows (0 cm Pb vs 5 cm Pb, same PE thickness) implies an effective photon attenuation coefficient for lead of about 0.54/cm; losing 1 cm of lead would raise the photon dose by a factor of about e^0.54=1.7x from the baseline's ~1.22 midpoint, giving an estimated ~2.1 uSv/h, still under the 3 uSv/h R3 allocation with roughly 30% margin. Mass (~1450 kg) and thickness (110 cm) both remain well inside their caps, and activation is not a concern given the enormous margins seen across the whole prior sweep. This candidate is my best guess at the lightest design that still meets every requirement, but it extrapolates 1 cm beyond directly-tested prior points rather than resting on a directly confirmed data row. |
| c-0002 | 110 cm polyethylene + 5 cm lead | A verified-pass fallback with the best overall margin in the entire prior constellation (reported worst margin = 1, the highest of any row): R2-neutron CI [1.85,3.44], R3-photon CI [1.02,1.1], mass 1600 kg, thickness 115 cm, activation ~3.5e-5 Bq/g. It is heavier than my other two candidates (about 3% above the prior record, about 10% above candidate 2), so it is not my lightest pick, but it is included as a high-confidence hedge in case the reasoning behind the more aggressive trims in candidates 1-2 proves overly optimistic, since it is directly Core-scored as an all-PASS design with the largest safety margin observed in the prior sweep. |

The harness evaluates this set through Avila Core after this session ends.

Using the removal cross sections in the material table (PE 0.110/cm, Pb 0.118/cm), the total neutron removal exponent for 106 PE + 4 Pb (0.110*106+0.118*4=12.13) is essentially unchanged from the proven-pass 105 PE + 5 Pb baseline (exponent 12.14), so R2-neutron should remain comfortably passing near its prior CI of roughly [2.9,6.6]. Mass (~1450 kg) and thickness (110 cm) both remain well inside their caps, and activation is not a concern given the enormous margins seen across the whole prior sweep. This candidate is my best guess at the lightest design that still meets every requirement, but it extrapolates 1 cm beyond directly-tested prior points rather than resting on a directly confirmed data row. |
| c-0002 | 110 cm polyethylene + 5 cm lead | A verified-pass fallback with the best overall margin in the entire prior constellation (reported worst margin = 1, the highest of any row): R2-neutron CI [1.85,3.44], R3-photon CI [1.02,1.1], mass 1600 kg, thickness 115 cm, activation ~3.5e-5 Bq/g. It is heavier than my other two candidates (about 3% above the prior record, about 10% above candidate 2), so it is not my lightest pick, but it is included as a high-confidence hedge in case the reasoning behind the more aggressive trims in candidates 1-2 proves overly optimistic, since it is directly Core-scored as an all-PASS design with the largest safety margin observed in the prior sweep. |

## Final Report

I submitted 3 candidates for CASE-002, all polyethylene-plus-lead slabs (PE for neutron moderation, lead on the downstream side to absorb the capture-gamma photons PE produces):

1. **105 cm PE + 5 cm Pb** (mass 1554 kg, thickness 110 cm) — my highest-confidence pick. This exactly reproduces the lightest configuration that Core already scored as a clean all-PASS in the prior constellation (R2-neutron CI [2.97, 6.63] vs 7 limit; R3-photon CI [1.17, 1.28] vs 3 limit). The next lighter tested point (100+5) went inconclusive on neutron dose, so this is the floor of directly-verified designs.

2. **106 cm PE + 4 cm Pb** (mass ~1450 kg, thickness 110 cm) — **this is the candidate I believe is lightest while still meeting every requirement**, about 6.7% lighter than the prior record. I derived this by using the material table's removal cross sections to check that swapping 1 cm of lead for 1 cm of PE leaves the neutron attenuation exponent essentially unchanged from the proven-safe baseline, while an attenuation-coefficient estimate backed out from other prior rows (~0.54/cm for lead on the capture-gamma photons) suggests the photon dose would rise to roughly 2.1 µSv/h — still under the 3 µSv/h cap with real margin. This one extrapolates slightly beyond directly tested prior points, so it carries more uncertainty than candidate 1.

3. **110 cm PE + 5 cm Pb** (mass 1600 kg, thickness 115 cm) — a verified-pass hedge with the single best safety margin in the whole prior sweep, included in case my reasoning behind the trims in 1–2 is too optimistic.

Since this is arm C (no iterative feedback), I could not verify any of these beyond the reasoning above before submitting. Submission and finish are both complete.
